copy.en:
Why do cities flood faster than the countryside?

In the countryside, soil soaks up rainwater! But cities are mostly cement, so they need drains to carry water away. When drains clog, nothing soaks or carries the water — floods come fast!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis bumaha sa lungsod kaysa sa bukid?

Sa bukid, sinisipsip ng lupa ang ulan! Pero sa lungsod, semento ang karamihan kaya kailangan ng kanal. Kapag barado ang kanal, walang sisipsip o magpapalabas ng tubig — mas mabilis bumaha!
copy.bis:
Ngano mas paspas mobaha sa siyudad kaysa sa bukid?

Sa bukid, suyopon sa yuta ang ulan! Apan sa siyudad, semento ang kadaghanan maong kinahanglan og kanal. Kung mababagan ang kanal, walay mosuyop o mopagawas — mas paspas mobaha!

copy.en: The Philippines gets many typhoons during the rainy season! That's why drains must be super clean before a typhoon hits — strong rain plus clogged drains equals easy flooding!
copy.tl: Maraming bagyo ang dumadaan sa Pilipinas tuwing tag-ulan! Kaya kailangang malinis ang mga kanal bago dumating ang bagyo — malakas na ulan at baradong kanal ay madaling pagbaha!
copy.bis: Daghan og bagyo ang moagi sa Pilipinas sa ting-ulan! Busa kinahanglan limpyo ang mga kanal una moabot ang bagyo — kusog nga ulan ug mababagan nga kanal dali ra mobaha!

copy.bis:
Mahimo bang sobra kabug-at ang usa ka humok nga panganod?

Oo! Ang dako nga puti nga panganod motimbang og gatusan ka tonelada — sama kabug-at sa daghang elepante! Naglutaw pa gihapon kay ang tubig nagkatag isip gagmay kaayo nga tulo sa hangin.

Which cloud is the tallest of them all?

The cumulonimbus is the tallest cloud type! It produces heavy rain, lightning, thunder, and sometimes hail.

Aling ulap ang pinakamataas sa lahat?

Ang cumulonimbus ay ang pinakamataas na uri ng ulap! Nagdudulot ito ng malakas na ulan, kidlat, kulog, at minsan ay hail.

copy.en: Carbon dioxide is invisible, with no color or smell, but it's all around us! It's the gas we breathe out. Even unseen, lots of it affects our world's warmth.
copy.tl: Walang kulay o amoy ang carbon dioxide kaya hindi natin nakikita, pero nasa hangin ito! Ito ang gas na inilalabas natin sa paghinga. Kahit hindi nakikita, marami nito ang nakakaapekto sa init ng mundo.

Is global warming caused by the ozone hole?

Nope, they are different! The ozone hole lets in UV rays that burn skin. The greenhouse effect is about heat trapped by gases. They have totally different causes!
copy.tl:
Ang pag-init ng mundo ba ay dahil sa ozone hole?

Hindi, magkaiba sila! Ang ozone hole ay tungkol sa UV rays na nakakasunog ng balat. Ang greenhouse effect naman ay tungkol sa init na nakukulong ng mga gas. Magkaiba ang dahilan nila!
copy.bis:

Dili, lahi sila! Ang ozone hole bahin sa UV rays nga makapaso sa panit. Ang greenhouse effect bahin sa kainit nga nadakpan sa mga gas. Lahi ang hinungdan sa duha!

What invisible gas comes out when wood, paper, or gasoline burns?

Carbon dioxide! It's one of the main gases released when these fuels burn — and you can't see it at all.

Carbon dioxide! Usa kini sa mga nag-unang gas nga mogawas kung masunog kini — ug dili nimo kini makita.

Coal is burned in power plants for electricity, oil is made into gasoline for vehicles, and natural gas is used for cooking and heating!

Ang karbon ay sinusunog sa power plant para sa kuryente, ang langis ay ginagawang gasolina para sa sasakyan, at ang natural gas ay para sa pagluluto at pag-init!
copy.bis:

Ang karbon gisunog sa power plant para sa kuryente, ang lana himoong gasolina para sa sakyanan, ug ang natural gas gigamit sa pagluto ug pagpainit!

How do waves break down our coastlines?

copy.tl:
Saan gustong magtago ang ipis?

Gustong-gusto ng ipis ang mainit at mamasa-masang lugar tulad ng kusina, ilalim ng lababo, at alkantarilya — doon sila nakakahanap ng pagkain at tubig.
copy.bis:
Asa ganahang magtago ang ipis?

Ganahan ang ipis sa init ug umog nga dapit sama sa kusina, ilalom sa lababo, ug kanal — didto sila makakita og pagkaon ug tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: days without water, and weeks without food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions surviving without water and food, but does not identify basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) or teach that these are required. It focuses on cockroach resilience, not on identifying needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cockroaches are super tough
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes toughness/survival ability but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment (e.g., mimicry, camouflage). No evolutionary adaptation is taught.

copy.en:
How long can a headless cockroach survive?

Cockroaches are super tough — they can survive weeks without a head, days without water, and weeks without food!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabubuhay ang ipis kahit walang ulo?

Ang ipis ay isa sa pinakamatibay na nilalang — kaya nitong mabuhay nang ilang linggo kahit walang ulo, ilang araw na walang tubig, at matagal na walang pagkain.
copy.bis:
Hangtod kanus-a mabuhi ang ipis bisan walay ulo?

Ang ipis usa sa pinakalig-on nga binuhat — makabuhi kini og pipila ka semana bisan walay ulo, pipila ka adlaw walay tubig, ug pipila ka semana walay pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The coco de mer has the biggest, heaviest seed in the world — one seed can weigh more than 15 kilograms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Record seed size is not a description of pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the biggest, heaviest seed in the world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: A seed superlative is not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en:
What plant has the biggest seed in the world?

The coco de mer has the biggest, heaviest seed in the world — one seed can weigh more than 15 kilograms, heavier than a baby!
copy.tl:
Aling halaman ang may pinakamalaking buto sa buong mundo?

Ang coco de mer ay may pinakamalaki at pinakamabigat na buto sa buong mundo — umaabot ng higit 15 kilo, mas mabigat pa sa isang sanggol!
copy.bis:
Unsang tanom ang adunay pinakadako nga liso sa kalibotan?

Ang coco de mer adunay pinakadako ug pinakabug-at nga liso sa tibuok kalibotan — moabot og kapin sa 15 ka kilo, mas bug-at pa sa usa ka masuso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The wide fronds of the coconut palm are woven into pawid, a natural roof that shields huts from rain and sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about useful things made from non-living materials. Coconut fronds are plant (living) material, not non-living. The card does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The wide fronds of the coconut palm are woven into pawid, a natural roof that shields huts from rain and sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant part (fronds) but does not describe observing outer parts of plants or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only uses fronds as a building material, so it is not direct support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The wide fronds of the coconut palm are woven into pawid, a natural roof that shields huts from rain and sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a human use of a plant part for shelter, but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is not direct support for this competency.

copy.en: The wide fronds of the coconut palm are woven into pawid, a natural roof that shields huts from rain and sun.
copy.tl: Ang malalapad na dahon ng niyog ay hinahabi upang gawing pawid — likas na atip na sumasanggalang sa bahay-kubo mula sa ulan at init.
copy.bis: Ang halapad nga dahon sa lubi ginahabol aron mahimong pawod, natural nga atop nga nanalipod sa balay gikan sa ulan ug init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coconut water isn't just water traveling up from the roots — it's a clear liquid that forms right inside the coconut as the seed develops.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Mentions roots only to reject them as the source of coconut water; does not teach leaves/roots/stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a clear liquid that forms right inside the coconut as the seed develops
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Liquid forming as a seed develops is adjacent to seed production; the card does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

copy.en:
Where does coconut water really come from?

Coconut water isn't just water traveling up from the roots — it's a clear liquid that forms right inside the coconut as the seed develops.
copy.tl:
Saan talaga galing ang buko juice?

Hindi lang tubig na dumaan sa ugat ang coconut water — malinaw na likido ito na nabubuo sa loob mismo ng niyog habang lumalaki ang buto.
copy.bis:
Asa gyud naggikan ang tubig sa lubi?

Ang tubig sa lubi dili lang tubig nga miagi sa gamot — usa kini ka klarong likido nga naporma sulod mismo sa lubi samtang nagtubo ang liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The coelacanth is an ancient fish scientists thought went extinct long ago — until a living one was actually caught in 1938!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that a coelacanth, an ancient fish, was found alive in 1938. It does not explain how fossils, biogeography, or comparative morphology support evolution, nor does it present any line of evidence for evolution. The living-fossil idea is only tangentially related to evolution evidence.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The coelacanth is an ancient fish scientists thought went extinct long ago — until a living one was actually caught in 1938!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a species that was thought extinct but found alive, which touches on extinction but does not discuss threats to biodiversity or how they lead to extinction. It does not support a class discussion on biodiversity threats and extinction.

copy.en:
Can a 'long-extinct' fish still be alive?

The coelacanth is an ancient fish scientists thought went extinct long ago — until a living one was actually caught in 1938!
copy.tl:
Puwede bang buhay pa pala ang isdang akala'y patay na?

Ang coelacanth ay lumang isda na akala ng mga siyentipiko ay matagal nang extinct — hanggang may nahuling buhay noong 1938!
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang buhi pa diay ang isda nga giisip nga napuo na?

Ang coelacanth usa ka karaan nga isda nga gihunahuna sa siyentista nga dugay na napuo — hangtod nay nadakpan nga buhi niadtong 1938!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cogon roots are boiled in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions roots as a plant part used in a folk remedy; it does not teach observing outer plant parts or their role in taking up water and nutrients.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cogon roots are boiled in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important; it is about a traditional herbal drink, not plant structure or function.

copy.en: In some parts of the Philippines, cogon roots are boiled in water as a traditional herbal drink — but this folk remedy should always be done with an adult's guidance.
copy.tl: Sa ilang lugar sa Pilipinas, pinapakuluan ang ugat ng cogon bilang tradisyonal na herbal na inumin—pero dapat laging may gabay ng nakatatanda ang gawaing ito.
copy.bis: Sa pipila ka dapit sa Pilipinas, gilat-an ang gamot sa kugon isip tradisyonal nga herbal nga ilimnon—apan kinahanglan kanunay nga giyahan sa hamtong ang buhat nga kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it weighs only about 32 to 40 grams
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions grams as a unit of mass, but it does not teach how to identify or appropriately use units in simple science activities. It simply states a weight in grams without explaining the unit, its relationship to other units, or any measurement activity. This is a factual statement using a unit, not instruction supporting the competency.

copy.en: The colasisi is super light — it weighs only about 32 to 40 grams, barely more than a few coins!
copy.tl: Napakagaan ng kulasisi — mga 32 hanggang 40 gramo lamang ang timbang nito!
copy.bis: Gaan kaayo ang kulasisi — mga 32 hangtod 40 ka gramo ra ang gibug-aton niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The colasisi has a short, rounded tail
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (tail) of an animal, but it does not identify the tail's role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of the competency. It only states the tail's shape and length, so it does not directly support the skill of identifying the role of body parts.

copy.en: The colasisi has a short, rounded tail — not a long one like some other parrots.
copy.tl: Ang kulasisi ay may maikli at bilog na buntot, hindi mahabang buntot.
copy.bis: Ang kulasisi adunay mubo ug lingin nga ikog, dili taas nga ikog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: depend on the warmth around them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions animals depending on environmental warmth (temperature), which is an abiotic factor, but it does not describe living things as biotic factors or classify light, water, temperature, and soil type as abiotic factors. It only touches on one abiotic influence without the required conceptual framing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold-blooded animals like snakes and lizards depend on the warmth around them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about how plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. The card is about cold-blooded animals basking in the sun, which is not about plant adaptation to unfavorable conditions and does not support this competency.

copy.en: Cold-blooded animals like snakes and lizards depend on the warmth around them, so they bask in the sun to warm up.
copy.tl: Ang mga hayop na cold-blooded, gaya ng ahas at butiki, ay umaasa sa init ng kapaligiran kaya nagbibilad sila sa araw para uminit.
copy.bis: Ang mga hayop nga cold-blooded, sama sa bitin ug tiki, nagsalig sa init sa palibot mao nga magpainit sila sa adlaw aron moinit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cold-blooded animals' body temperature rises when it's warm outside and falls when it's cold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature as an environmental condition affecting a living thing, but it does not teach the concept of biotic vs. abiotic factors or classify temperature as an abiotic factor. It only describes a physiological response, not the ecosystem factor framework.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cold-blooded animals' body temperature rises when it's warm outside and falls when it's cold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a temperature-dependent body process, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not explicitly teach that living things respond to stimuli; it only states a fact about cold-blooded animals.

copy.en:
Why does a lizard feel warm in the sun?

Because cold-blooded animals' body temperature rises when it's warm outside and falls when it's cold.
copy.tl:
Bakit umiinit ang katawan ng butiki sa araw?

Dahil ang temperatura ng katawan ng mga hayop na malamig ang dugo ay tumataas kapag mainit at bumababa kapag malamig ang paligid.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga moinit ang lawas sa halas sa adlaw?

Tungod kay ang temperatura sa lawas sa mga mananap nga bugnaw ug dugo motaas kung init ug monaog kung bugnaw ang palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most vaccines must stay between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius to work
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions degrees Celsius as a temperature unit, but it does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in simple science activities. The content is about vaccine cold chain storage, not about unit identification or measurement practice.

copy.en: Most vaccines must stay between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius to work — the 'cold chain' is the system of fridges and cool containers keeping them right from factory to clinic!
copy.tl: Kailangang itago ang karamihan ng bakuna sa 2-8°C para gumana ito — ang 'cold chain' ang sistema ng mga refrigerator at insulated na sisidlan na nagpapanatili ng tamang temperatura mula sa paggawa hanggang gamitin!
copy.bis: Kinahanglang ibutang ang kadaghanan sa bakuna sa 2-8°C aron molihok kini — ang 'cold chain' mao ang sistema sa mga refrigerator ug insulated nga sudlanan nga nagbantay sa tamang temperatura gikan sa paghimo hangtod gamiton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all deserts are hot! There are also cold deserts like Antarctica that get almost no rain.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature and rain, which are weather characteristics, but it uses them to describe desert types rather than teaching how to identify basic weather characteristics. It does not address air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, or cloud cover, and provides no instructional support for the competency's skill.

copy.en: Not all deserts are hot! There are also cold deserts like Antarctica that get almost no rain.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng disyerto ay mainit! May malalamig na disyerto rin tulad ng Antarctica na halos walang ulan.
copy.bis: Dili tanan nga desyerto init! Adunay bugnaw nga desyerto sama sa Antarctica nga halos walay ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: people tend to catch colds and flu more often during the rainy, cooler months
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes a health effect of rainy/cool weather but does not describe how weather changes affect daily activities or explain dangerous weather types (e.g., storms, floods). It only tangentially relates weather to illness.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: during the rainy, cooler months
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a rainy/cool season but does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. It only states a health correlation with one season.

copy.en: In the Philippines, people tend to catch colds and flu more often during the rainy, cooler months.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, mas madalas magkasipon at magka-trangkaso ang mga tao tuwing tag-ulan at malamig na panahon.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang mga tawo kasagaran mas magsip-on ug magtrangkaso panahon sa ting-ulan ug bugnaw nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plenty of rest and lots of water are your best friends for recovering.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card advises rest and water for recovering from a cold or flu. It does not teach identifying basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). Water is mentioned but only as a recovery aid, not as a general basic need, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Got a cold or the flu? Plenty of rest and lots of water are your best friends for recovering.
copy.tl: May sipon o trangkaso ka? Ang sapat na pahinga at maraming tubig ang makakatulong sa iyong paggaling.
copy.bis: Naay sip-on o trangkaso ka? Ang igong pahuway ug daghang tubig ang makatabang sa imong pagkaayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A colloid is a mix where very tiny particles spread evenly and never settle, like milk or fog!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes colloids, a type of mixture, but the competency specifically targets uniform and non-uniform mixtures with examples of solutions and suspensions. The card does not describe solutions or suspensions, nor does it classify mixtures as uniform or non-uniform. It only mentions that colloid particles are larger than solution particles, which is background comparison, not direct instruction on the competency's stated skill.

copy.en: A colloid is a mix where very tiny particles spread evenly and never settle, like milk or fog! They are bigger than solution particles but too small to see.
copy.tl: Ang colloid ay timpla kung saan napakaliliit na particles ay kumakalat nang pantay at hindi lumulubog, gaya ng gatas o fog! Mas malaki sila kaysa sa solution pero hindi nakikita.
copy.bis: Ang colloid usa ka sagol diin gagmay kaayong particles nagkatag nga patas ug dili molubog, sama sa gatas o gabon! Mas dako sila kaysa sa solution apan dili makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A colloid is a mixture where particles are too small to settle but too big for a true solution
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes colloids, a type of mixture, but the competency specifically targets uniform and non-uniform mixtures with examples of solutions and suspensions. Colloids are not solutions or suspensions, and the card does not address the uniform/non-uniform distinction or the named examples, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A colloid is a mixture where particles are too small to settle but too big for a true solution, like milk or fog. They stay spread out a long time!
copy.tl: Ang colloid ay mixture kung saan ang mga particle ay sobrang liit para lumapag pero malaki para maging true solution, gaya ng gatas. Nananatili silang sabog nang matagal!
copy.bis: Ang colloid usa ka mixture diin ang mga particle gagmay kaayo aron molingkod apan dako kaayo aron mahimong true solution, sama sa gatas. Magpabilin silang sabwag og dugay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects get their colour by absorbing some light colours and reflecting others.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains color perception via absorption and reflection of light, but G8-F-11 specifically requires guided investigations describing/illustrating reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card does not address mirrors, refraction, or the required investigation activities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects get their colour by absorbing some light colours and reflecting others.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: G3-F-6 focuses on exploring sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, and its uses. The card describes how objects reflect/absorb light to produce color, which is a light behavior, but it does not involve guided activities, sources of light, or everyday uses as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why does a red apple look red?

Objects get their colour by absorbing some light colours and reflecting others. A red apple absorbs all colours except red, which it reflects back to your eyes!
copy.tl:
Bakit pula ang itsura ng mansanas?

Ang mga bagay ay nagkakaroon ng kulay dahil sinisipsip nito ang ibang kulay ng liwanag at sinasalamin ang iba. Ang pulang mansanas ay sinisipsip ang lahat maliban sa pula, na sinasalamin nito pabalik sa iyong mga mata!
copy.bis:
Nganong pula ang hitsura sa mansanas?

Ang mga butang nagkuha og kolor tungod kay gisipsip niini ang ubang kolor sa suga ug gipakita ang uban. Ang pula nga mansanas gisipsip ang tanan gawas sa pula, nga gipakita niini pabalik sa imong mga mata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Color alone isn't always reliable for identifying a mineral because one mineral can come in many different colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about exploring/collecting rocks and describing their similarities/differences using features like texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card discusses mineral color unreliability, which is a caution about a feature but does not instruct students to observe, collect, or describe rocks. It is background knowledge about minerals, not direct support for the rock observation/description skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Color alone isn't always reliable for identifying a mineral because one mineral can come in many different colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: classify common rocks from provided samples using a simple rock classification system, such as a dichotomous key
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about classifying common rocks using a simple classification system such as a dichotomous key. The card only states that color is unreliable for mineral identification; it does not teach classification of rocks or use of a classification system. It is related vocabulary but provides no direct instructional support for classifying rocks.

copy.en:
Why can't we always trust a mineral's color?

Color alone isn't always reliable for identifying a mineral because one mineral can come in many different colors!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi laging maaasahan ang kulay ng mineral?

Hindi laging maaasahan ang kulay sa pagkilala ng mineral dahil ang isang mineral ay pwedeng magkaroon ng iba't ibang kulay!
copy.bis:
Ngano dili kanunay kasaligan ang kolor sa mineral?

Ang kolor lang dili kanunay kasaligan sa pag-ila sa mineral kay ang usa ka mineral mahimong adunay lainlaing kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As metal gets hotter, its glowing color changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a color change with temperature, involving heat and light, but it does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it teach the concept of light, sound, or heat energy as forms of energy. It only illustrates a phenomenon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As metal gets hotter, its glowing color changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions glowing/light from hot metal, but it does not describe sources of light or their use in everyday situations. It is about color change with temperature, not about identifying light sources or their uses.

copy.en: As metal gets hotter, its glowing color changes! It starts red at 700°C, then turns orange, yellow, and finally bright white hot above 1,400°C.
copy.tl: Habang umiinit ang metal, nagbabago ang kulay ng liwanag nito! Nagsisimula itong pula sa 700°C, tapos orange, dilaw, at sa wakas puti sa 1,400°C.
copy.bis: Samang mo-init ang metal, nagbag-o ang kolor sa suga niini! Nagsugod kini nga pula sa 700°C, dayon orange, dalag, ug sa katapusan puti sa 1,400°C.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one of the closest living relatives of primates like monkeys and humans
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why humans are classified under Class Mammalia and the Order Primates
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that colugos are close relatives of primates; it does not explain why humans are classified under Class Mammalia and the Order Primates, nor does it provide any taxonomic reasoning or characteristics.

copy.en:
What animal is a close cousin of monkeys?

The colugo! Scientists say it's one of the closest living relatives of primates like monkeys and humans.
copy.tl:
Anong hayop ang malapit na kamag-anak ng unggoy?

Ang colugo! Ayon sa mga siyentista, isa ito sa pinakamalapit na kamag-anak ng mga primate gaya ng unggoy at tao.
copy.bis:
Unsang hayopa ang suod nga kabanay sa unggoy?

Ang colugo! Sumala sa mga siyentista, usa kini sa labing duol nga kabanay sa mga primate sama sa unggoy ug tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The colugo has a wide flap of skin called a patagium
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part of an animal but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The colugo has a wide flap of skin called a patagium
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physical feature but does not explain how the colugo has changed to better suit its environment, so it does not directly support the adaptation competency.

copy.en: The colugo has a wide flap of skin called a patagium that stretches from its neck to the tip of its tail and between its legs.
copy.tl: May malapad na balat ang kagwang na tinatawag na patagium, na umaabot mula leeg hanggang dulo ng buntot at sa pagitan ng mga paa.
copy.bis: Ang kagwang adunay lapad nga panit nga gitawag patagium, gikan sa liog hangtod tumoy sa ikog ug sa tunga-tunga sa mga tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Barnacles stick to a whale's skin to hitch a ride into food-rich waters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hitch a ride into food-rich waters, while the whale barely notices
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the whale barely notices — a classic example of commensalism

assignedReviews.reason: Neither helped nor harmed is not explaining how an interaction brings good or harm.

copy.en:
What is commensalism?

It's when one animal gets a free ride, shelter, or food scraps from a bigger animal — who doesn't even notice or mind!
copy.tl:
Ano ang commensalism?

Ito ay kapag may hayop na nakikinabang sa libreng sakay, silungan, o tira-tirang pagkain mula sa mas malaking hayop — na hindi man lang ito napapansin!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang commensalism?

Kini mao kon ang usa ka mananap makabenepisyo og libreng sakay, silungan, o salin nga pagkaon gikan sa mas dakong mananap — nga wala gani makamatikod!

copy.en:
What is 'phoresy' in animals?

In phoresy, tiny creatures hitch a ride on a bigger animal to travel—like insects clinging to a bird or fly, without bothering their ride!
copy.tl:
Ano ang 'phoresy' sa mga hayop?

Sa phoresy, sumasakay ang maliliit na nilalang sa mas malaking hayop para makalipat ng lugar—tulad ng insektong dumidikit sa ibon o langaw, hindi naaabala ang sasakyan nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang 'phoresy' sa mga hayop?

Sa phoresy, mosakay ang gagmayng binuhat sa mas dako nga hayop aron mobalhin og dapit—sama sa insekto nga motapot sa langgam o langaw, nga walay samok sa gisakyan!

copy.en: In commensalism, the host isn't harmed because the commensal doesn't take its food or energy — it only takes the extras, leftovers, or unneeded space!
copy.tl: Sa commensalism, hindi nasasaktan ang host dahil hindi kinukuha ng commensal ang pagkain o lakas nito — kumukuha lang ito ng sobra, tira, o espasyong hindi kailangan!
copy.bis: Sa commensalism, dili madaot ang host kay wala kuhaa sa commensal ang pagkaon o kusog niini — mokuha lang kini sa sobra, salin, o luna nga wala kinahanglana!

copy.en:
Does an orchid harm its tree?

Some orchids grow on a tree's branch just to reach sunlight — they never take the tree's nutrients. Scientists call this commensalism.
copy.tl:
Nasasaktan ba ang puno sa orkidya?

Tumutubo ang ilang orkidya sa sanga ng puno para lang maabot ang sikat ng araw — hindi nito kinukuha ang sustansya ng puno. Tinatawag itong komensalismo.
copy.bis:
Naunsa ba ang kahoy sa orkid?

Ang ubang orkid motubo sa sanga sa kahoy aron lang maabot ang silaw sa adlaw — wala niini kuhaa ang sustansya sa kahoy. Gitawag kini nga komensalismo.

copy.en:
What keeps a motor's coil spinning in one direction?

A motor has a part called a commutator that switches the current direction so the coil keeps spinning the same way!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapapatuloy sa pag-ikot ng coil sa iisang direksyon?

May bahaging tinatawag na commutator ang motor na nagbabago ng direksyon ng kuryente para patuloy na umikot ang coil sa iisang direksyon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagpadayon sa pagliko sa coil sa usa ka direksyon?

Ang motor adunay bahin nga gitawag ug commutator nga magbalhin sa direksyon sa kuryente aron padayon nga moliko ang coil sa usa ka direksyon!

copy.bis: Unang gigamit sa China, ang kompas adunay magnetikong dagom nga kanunay motudlo sa amihanan — nakatabang sa mga marino nga dili masaag bisan layo sa dagat!

copy.bis: Ang dagom sa compass motudlo sa magnetic north — dili sa tinuod nga amihanan sa globo! Kinahanglan mag-adjust ang mga marinero sa gamay nga gilay-on.

copy.bis: Ang dagom sa compass usa ka gamay nga magnet nga kanunay nagtudlo sa amihanan aron makatabang nato sa pagpangita sa direksyon!

copy.en:
Why do modern cameras and telescopes combine concave and convex lenses?

They combine them to make sharper images! The concave lens helps fix certain light errors.
copy.tl:
Bakit pinagsasama ng mga modernong kamera at teleskopyo ang concave at convex lenses?

Pinagsasama sila para mas linaw ang litrato! Ang concave lens ang tumutulong na maitama ang ilang mali sa liwanag.
copy.bis:
Ngano gisagol sa modernong kamera ug teleskopyo ang concave ug convex lenses?

Gisagol sila aron mas klaro ang hulagway! Ang concave lens maoy motabang aron matul-id ang pipila ka sayop sa kahayag.

copy.bis: Ang sumbanan nga nota sa musika nga A4 adunay frequency nga 440 Hz, nga gigamit sa pag-tune sa mga instrumento!

copy.en:
Does concrete harden by drying out?

Nope! It hardens through a chemical reaction between cement and water. That's why it must be kept damp while gaining strength!
copy.tl:
Natutuyo ba ang konkreto para tumigas?

Hindi! Tumitigas ito dahil sa reaksyong kemikal ng semento at tubig. Kaya kailangan itong basang-basa habang lumalakas!
copy.bis:
Namala ba ang konkreto aron mogahi?

Dili! Mogahi kini tungod sa reaksyong kemikal sa semento ug tubig. Mao nga kinahanglan basa-basa kini samtang nagkakusog!

copy.en:
Is hardened concrete strong when you push and pull it?

It’s very strong when pushed (compression) but weak when pulled apart (tension), so it can crack when stretched!
copy.tl:
Matibay ba ang tigas na konkreto kapag idinidiin at hinihila?

Napakalakas ito kapag idinidiin (compression) pero mahina kapag hinihila (tension), kaya naluluray ito kapag binanat!
copy.bis:
Lig-on ba ang gahi nga konkreto kon ipiton ug biraon?

Kusog kaayo kini kon ipiton (compression) apan huyang kon biraon (tension), busa daling mabuak kon batakon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reducing static electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a real-world application of static charge (hair conditioner neutralizing static) but does not involve investigating effects using common materials such as a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons as required by the competency. It provides background knowledge about static attraction but does not directly support the investigation skill.

copy.en: Hair conditioner contains positively charged (cationic) compounds! These are attracted to negatively charged hair, smoothing the surface and reducing static electricity.
copy.tl: Ang hair conditioner ay naglalaman ng positively charged (cationic) compounds! Naakit ang mga ito sa negatively charged na buhok, na nagpapakinis at nagpapababa ng static electricity.
copy.bis: Ang hair conditioner adunay positively charged (cationic) compounds! Nadani kini sa negatively charged nga buhok, nagpapahapsay sa nawong ug nagpababa sa static electricity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In conduction, heat moves when two things touch directly! That's why a metal spoon in hot soup makes your hand feel warm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of conduction (metal spoon in hot soup) but does not identify it as advantageous or disadvantageous, nor does it address convection or radiation. It only illustrates the mechanism of conduction, not the competency's focus on classifying examples as advantageous/disadvantageous.

copy.en: In conduction, heat moves when two things touch directly! That's why a metal spoon in hot soup makes your hand feel warm.
copy.tl: Sa conduction, lumilipat ang init kapag nagkadikit ang dalawang bagay! Kaya kapag hinawakan mo ang metal na kutsara sa mainit na sabaw, maiinitan ang kamay mo.
copy.bis: Sa conduction, molabay ang init kung magkadikit ang duha ka butang! Mao nga kung kuptan nimo ang puthaw nga kutsara sa init nga sabaw, mainitan ang imong kamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conduction is heat moving through direct touching! Insulation is like a shield that slows this heat down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines conduction and describes insulation, which is background knowledge for the competency. However, it does not identify any advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, which is the specific skill required by G7-F-9.

copy.en: Conduction is heat moving through direct touching! Insulation is like a shield that slows this heat down.
copy.tl: Ang kondaksyon ay paglipat ng init sa pamamagitan ng direktang pagdikit. Pinapabagal naman ito ng insulasyon!
copy.bis: Ang kondaksyon mao ang paglihok sa kainit pinaagi sa direktang paghikap, ug ang insulasyon magpahinay niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In conduction, heat spreads through direct contact, especially in solids!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains what conduction is and gives an example (metal spoon in hot soup), but it does not identify the example as advantageous or disadvantageous, nor does it address convection or radiation. It provides background knowledge needed to later classify examples, but does not directly teach the competency's action of identifying advantageous/disadvantageous examples.

copy.en: In conduction, heat spreads through direct contact, especially in solids! For example, a whole metal spoon gets hot when its tip is dipped in hot soup.
copy.tl: Sa conduction, kumakalat ang init sa tuwirang pagdikit, lalo na sa solids! Halimbawa, umiinit ang buong metal na kutsara kapag inilubog ang dulo sa mainit na sabaw.
copy.bis: Sa conduction, mokaylap ang init pinaagi sa direktang pagdikit, ilabi na sa solids! Pananglitan, moinit ang tibuok metal nga kutsara kung ituslob ang tumoy sa init nga sabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it easily—like copper and other metals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines what a conductor is, which is background knowledge for identifying conducting materials, but it does not teach designing or constructing a simple circuit, nor the process of testing materials to identify conductors and insulators as required by the competency.

copy.en: A conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it easily—like copper and other metals!
copy.tl: Ang konduktor ay materyal na madaling pinagdadaluyan ng kuryente, gaya ng tanso at iba pang metal!
copy.bis: Ang konduktor usa ka materyal nga sayon nga giagian sa kuryente, sama sa tumbaga ug uban pang metal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metals and water let electricity flow through them easily! Because of this, we call them conductors.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that metals and water are conductors, which is background knowledge about conductivity. However, the competency requires designing and constructing a simple electrical circuit to identify conductors and insulators. The card does not address circuit construction or the identification process, so it only provides prerequisite knowledge.

copy.en: Metals and water let electricity flow through them easily! Because of this, we call them conductors.
copy.tl: Ang mga metal at tubig ay madaling magpadaloy ng kuryente! Kaya naman tinatawag silang mga konduktor.
copy.bis: Ang mga metal ug tubig sayon magpaagi sa kuryente! Mao nga gitawag silang mga konduktor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they have zero resistance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions zero resistance but does not address current, voltage, or series/parallel circuits, nor any investigation to infer their relationship. It is only tangentially related to resistance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: super strong magnetic fields
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions strong magnetic fields produced by superconductors, but does not teach properties of magnets, how magnets affect other magnets, or interactions with different materials. No guided investigation content is present.

copy.en:
Why are superconductors so cool and useful?

When super cold, they have zero resistance! They create super strong magnetic fields with no energy loss, powering MRI machines, maglev trains, and particle accelerators.
copy.tl:
Bakit ang galing ng mga superconductor?

Kapag napakalamig, zero ang resistance nila! Gumagawa sila ng napakalakas na magnetic field nang walang energy loss, kaya ginagamit sa MRI machines, maglev trains, at particle accelerators.
copy.bis:
Nganong nindot kaayo ang mga superconductor?

Kung bugnaw kaayo, zero ang resistance nila! Naghimo sila ug super strong magnetic field nga walay energy loss, mao nga gigamit sa MRI machines, maglev trains, ug particle accelerators.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a conductor and gives copper as an example, which is background knowledge for testing materials in a circuit. It does not address designing or constructing a simple circuit, nor using it to identify conductive and non-conductive materials from the environment, which are the core actions of the competency.

copy.en:
What do we call a material that lets electricity flow easily through it?

A conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it! Metals like copper are great examples.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa materyal na nagpapadaloy ng kuryente nang madali?

Ang konduktor ay materyal na nagpapadaloy ng kuryente! Ang mga metal gaya ng tanso (copper) ay magandang halimbawa.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa materyal nga nagpasayon sa pag-agi sa kuryente?

Ang konduktor kay materyal nga nagpaagi sa kuryente! Ang mga metal nga sama sa tanso (copper) maayong pananglitan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conductors like copper and other metals let electricity pass through easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about conductors (metals let electricity pass) but does not teach designing/constructing a circuit or using it to test and identify conducting vs non-conducting materials, which is the core action of the competency. It is useful background knowledge only.

copy.en: Conductors like copper and other metals let electricity pass through easily, which is why wires are made from them!
copy.tl: Ang mga konduktor gaya ng tanso at ibang metal ay nagpapadaloy ng kuryente nang madali, kaya ginagawa silang alambre!
copy.bis: Ang mga konduktor sama sa tumbaga ug uban pang metal magpaagi sa kuryente dali ra, mao nga ginahimo silang alambre!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conductors are materials with high thermal conductivity, so heat travels through them quickly and easily.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about thermal conductivity of materials, a physics topic. It does not address how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conductors are materials with high thermal conductivity, so heat travels through them quickly and easily.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heat conduction in materials, not interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bringing good or harm. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Conductors are materials with high thermal conductivity, so heat travels through them quickly and easily.
copy.tl: Ang conductors ay mga materyales na may mataas na thermal conductivity, kaya mabilis at madaling dumaan ang heat sa kanila.
copy.bis: Ang conductors kay mga materyales nga adunay taas nga thermal conductivity, mao nga paspas ug sayon moagi ang heat kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a closed system, total energy never changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the general principle of conservation of energy in a closed system, but the competency specifically requires describing conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as objects falling. The card gives no gravity context or everyday example, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: In a closed system, total energy never changes! If it drops in one form, it rises in another by the exact same amount. Energy just swaps forms!
copy.tl: Sa isang saradong sistema, hindi nagbabago ang kabuuang enerhiya! Kung bumaba sa isang anyo, tataas sa iba nang eksaktong kasingdami. Nagpapalitan lang ng anyo ang enerhiya!
copy.bis: Sa usa ka sirado nga sistema, dili mausab ang kinatibuk-ang enerhiya! Kung mokunhod sa usa ka porma, motaas sa lain sa eksakto nga gidaghanon. Nagbaylo lang og porma ang enerhiya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists divided the sky into 88 official constellations
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of official constellations. It does not explain why ancient cultures relied on constellations for directions or seasons, which is the core of G6-E-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every single star belongs to one of these 88 regions.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and constellations but does not involve guided observation or description of celestial objects as required by G3-E-6.

copy.en:
How many official constellations cover the entire sky?

Scientists divided the sky into 88 official constellations — like provinces of the sky! Every single star belongs to one of these 88 regions.
copy.tl:
Ilan ang opisyal na konstelasyon na sumasakop sa buong langit?

Hinati ng mga siyentipiko ang langit sa 88 opisyal na konstelasyon — parang mga probinsya ng langit! Bawat bituin ay nasa isa sa 88 rehiyong ito.
copy.bis:
Pila ka opisyal nga konstelasyon ang naglukop sa tibuok langit?

Gibahin sa mga siyentista ang langit sa 88 ka opisyal nga konstelasyon — morag mga probinsya sa langit! Ang matag bituon naa sa usa sa 88 ka rehiyon.
